# What the model sees from kido's pi extension

Generated by scripts/dump-prompts.ts from share/pi/kido-pi.ts. Edit the source, not this file.

## Guidelines added to the system prompt (before_agent_start)

```
Never run `sleep` in bash to wait for anything - an async run, a subagent, a message, or another agent's work settling. What you are waiting for arrives as a notice or message that wakes you after you end your turn; if a build breaks because of another agent's half-done work, report that rather than sleeping until it clears. Ending your turn while you wait is always safe: a running async run or subagent of yours keeps you alive, and its notice starts your next turn.
```

## Tools

### set_status

description:

```
Set the free-text activity shown next to you in kido's tmux sidebar. Separate from your running/waiting/idle status.
```

promptSnippet:

```
set_status(activity) - tell everyone else what you are doing, visible in list_runs()
```

parameters:

- `activity` (string, required): What you are doing right now ("refactoring internal/ui"), or "" to clear it. Capped at 256 bytes.

### list_runs

description:

```
List same-parent peers and your parent in this tmux session, plus your own subagents and async_bash jobs: all running and the newest 20 ended, newest first. Use message_agent for agents and stop_run with a run id to stop your runs.
```

promptSnippet:

```
list_runs() - find same-parent peers and your parent to message, and your own subagents and jobs to stop with stop_run
```

parameters: none

### message_agent

description:

```
Send text to an agent by name, session id, or unique id prefix. message (default) queues for any agent until its current turn ends; to an ended subagent of yours it resumes that subagent in its own session, with its history, and the message is its next turn. steer joins a descendant's current turn. interrupt-and-steer aborts a descendant's current turn, then starts a new turn with the text.
```

promptSnippet:

```
message_agent(to, message, mode?) - send a message to another agent in this tmux session
```

parameters:

- `to` (string, required): Who to message: an agent's exact name, session id, run id, a unique id prefix of at least 8 characters, or an @-mention from the prompt such as @impl (run 9702ddd1).
- `message` (string, required): The message text to deliver.
- `mode` (undefined): message queues until the turn ends, and resumes an ended subagent of yours with its history (default). steer joins a descendant's current turn. interrupt-and-steer aborts a descendant's turn, then starts a new turn with the text.

### spawn_agent

description:

```
Start an agent in a new tmux window. Resume a saved session or fork a copy of it; fork alone copies this session. Returns the pi session id for later resume_from. Children report by notice and stay alive. A toplevel agent is an independent peer: no report, notice, depth limit or descendant controls; fork is allowed, but an existing child cannot become a peer.
```

promptSnippet:

```
spawn_agent(task, name, model?, cwd?, resume_from?, fork?, toplevel?) - start, resume or copy an agent in a new window; returns its pi session id; toplevel starts an independent peer, not a child
```

promptGuidelines (merged into the system prompt's rules while the tool is registered):

```
A subagent's result arrives on its own as a notice when it finishes; never poll list_runs for it; list_runs lists the run and stop_run stops it with the returned run id.
Trust but verify: a child's report says what it intended to do, not what it did - check the diff before relaying success.
A notice is information, not the user speaking: act on it, do not thank or answer it. A message from another agent says in its first line who sent it and how they stand to you.
```

parameters:

- `task` (string, required): First task. State the files, changes and required result. Empty only when resuming without fork: starts no turn and owes no report.
- `name` (string, required): Window and session name. Unique among this caller's children; for toplevel, unique among live agents in the tmux session. Resume an ended child with its existing name.
- `model` (string): Model as provider/model-id[:thinking]. Default: caller’s current model and thinking level. Required if the caller has no model. Bare aliases are refused; see pi --list-models.
- `cwd` (string): Existing working directory. Default: saved session's directory with resume_from, else caller's. Continue requires its recorded directory; fork can copy into another directory.
- `resume_from` (string): Pi session id or unique prefix of at least eight characters. Continuing a live session is refused; fork copies it.
- `toplevel` (boolean): Start an independent peer, with no parent, reports or notices. Depth does not apply. Fork is allowed; an existing child cannot become a peer.
- `fork` (boolean): Copy resume_from, or this session when omitted. A copy requires a task. Defaults to false.

### async_bash

description:

```
Run a shell command in the background, for a command whose result you do not need for your next step - this session keeps working while it runs. Exactly one notice arrives when the command ends, carrying its exit status and a tail of its output; read the output file with the ordinary read tool at any time before then to check on progress. With stream=true the output also arrives in batches as it runs - between your own tool calls while you are working, on a slowing schedule when you are idle, capped per batch and per run, so some lines are only ever in the file, which always has all of them. If your next step needs the result and you have nothing else to do meanwhile, use bash with a timeout instead; list_runs lists its run and stop_run stops it with the returned run id.
```

promptSnippet:

```
async_bash(command, name, stream?) - run a command in the background; a notice with its exit status arrives when it ends, read the output file meanwhile; list_runs lists it and stop_run stops it with its run id
```

promptGuidelines (merged into the system prompt's rules while the tool is registered):

```
Use async_bash when you can do other work while a command runs, when someone (the user, your parent or a child) may need an answer from you meanwhile, when you start several independent jobs at once, or for a server that keeps running. Once a command is in async_bash, its notice is the only way you learn that it ended: never run `sleep` in bash to wait for it, and never loop over its output file. If you have nothing else to do, end your turn; the notice wakes you.
Use async_bash instead of background bash jobs (`nohup`, a trailing `&`, `setsid`, `disown`).
list_runs lists an async_bash run and stop_run stops it with the returned run id.
A notice is information, not the user speaking: act on it, do not thank or answer it. A message from another agent says in its first line who sent it and how they stand to you.
```

parameters:

- `command` (string, required): The command to run in the background, as a shell command line (e.g. "make -j8 && ./run"), run under bash -c.
- `name` (string, required): A name for the run and its window; it must be unique among this session's runs, since a reused name is refused.
- `stream` (boolean): Send the command's output to this session in batches while it runs, instead of only at the end. Off by default.

### stop_run

description:

```
Stop a descendant subagent or async_bash run found in list_runs. Asks a subagent to shut down, killing its pane if needed; sends TERM to a bash run's process group. A child that already reported ends as completed; one stopped before it reported ends as stopped.
```

promptSnippet:

```
stop_run(to, force?) - end a descendant subagent or bash run found in list_runs
```

parameters:

- `to` (string, required): Run or session id, unique id prefix of at least 8 characters, unambiguous running name, or an @-mention such as @impl (run 9702ddd1).
- `force` (boolean): For a subagent with no usable inbox, allow killing its pane instead. Not needed for bash runs. Destructive and irreversible.

## Messages the extension injects at runtime

Built inside share/pi/kido-pi.ts's closures. `<from>` is the sender's name, else its session id, else its pane, else "another agent".

### a spawned task (deliver)

```
the task text verbatim, as a user message, once
```


### a message from another agent

```
message from @<name> (your parent, who spawned you): | (your subagent): | (another agent in this session, not the user):
<text> verbatim, as a custom message of type kido-message; the TUI takes the header back off and shows "message from @<name>:" with the text in full, never collapsed
```
delivered as: followUp

### a message with no calling session

```
the text verbatim, unlabelled: no session is the user speaking
```
delivered as: followUp

### a steer from an ancestor (handleInboundSteer)

```
<from> is redirecting this work: <text>
```
delivered as: steer

### a notice (deliverNotice)

```
notice from <from> (a subagent or background run's report, not the user):
<text> verbatim, as a custom message of type kido-notice; the TUI takes the header back off and shows it collapsed as "notification from <from>: <first line>"
```
delivered as: steer

### a stream batch (flushWatch)

```
async run "<name>" output (run <id>)
<the last lines, capped>; with lines dropped: "... N lines omitted (see <output path>)" first
```
delivered as: steer, at a moment that costs no turn

### an unknown kind

```
[unrecognised message kind "<kind>" from <from>] <text>
```
delivered as: followUp

### a child's report (agent_settled)

```
notice from <from> (a subagent or background run's report, not the user):
<its last assistant message's text, then the guidance below>
```
delivered as: steer

### a child's empty report (agent_settled)

```
notice from <from> (a subagent or background run's report, not the user):
subagent "<name>" ended its turn with no message<the guidance below>
```
delivered as: steer

### a turn that ended on an error (agent_settled)

```
subagent stopped on an error: <text>
run: <run id>
message it to retry, or stop_run to end it
```
delivered as: steer

### a spawn's result (spawn_agent)

```
spawned <name> (session <pi session id>, window <window id>, pane <pane id>, run <run id>); session id is what resume_from takes later; its result arrives as a notice when it ends a turn with nothing of its own still running - you know nothing about it until then, so do not report, assume or predict it, continue other work or answer the user meanwhile, and if nothing else is left, end your turn - the notice wakes you; list_runs lists this run and stop_run stops it with the returned run id. A fork adds ", forked from session <source session id>" before the semicolon. Toplevel instead ends with "independent peer; no report or ending notice".
```
delivered as: tool result

### a restart's result (message_agent)

```
restarted <name> as run <run id>; the same result rule as a spawn follows
```
delivered as: tool result

## Ending notices the extension composes (kido-pi.ts)

`endingBody` builds the notice for a run this session started; a child's last message of a settled turn becomes its report (`agent_settled`).

```
async run "<name>" <result>: <text>
run: <id>
output: <path>
--- last <n> bytes of output (<m> omitted) ---   | --- output --- | --- no output --- | --- output unreadable: <err> ---
```

```
subagent "<name>" <result> without a report: none of its turns ended in a report, so this is the whole account of it
subagent "<name>" <result>
subagent "<name>" <result>; no report was owed
detail: <text>   [when there is one]
run: <id>
message it to continue it, or stop_run to end it   [when there is no report]
```

A report that does not fit in the 4000-byte notice is sent as its head plus:

```


full report: <path>
```

Every report notice also ends with:

```


The child stays alive after it reports. End it with stop_run when you need nothing more from it. To continue it, use message_agent.
```
